title: Secure a loose trouser hem
instruction: Secure the loose trouser hem with the safety pin, with its point safely enclosed.
setup: An inside-out cotton trouser cuff, about 440 mm in circumference and 240 mm long, with a visible width of 180 mm when draped, rests over a 140 x 190 x 60 mm wooden sewing support inserted between its faces. The 20 mm turned front hem overhangs the support by 46 mm toward the left arm; its middle 100 mm of stitching is loose. The back stays below the support. An ordinary 75 mm steel safety pin lies open on a 20 x 40 x 15 mm wooden tool rest toward the right arm, with its coil overhanging the rest by 25 mm. Both hands start open.
scoring: 1.0 if the pin passes through both front and hem layers within the loose central 100 mm, returns through them to the surface, and closes with its point inside the shield; the hem remains secured after a three-second release. 0.5 if both layers are threaded but the pin is still open or held; 0.25 if a correct layer remains partly threaded on the shaft. Otherwise 0. Pinning outside that loose section or through the back of the leg, more than four punctures, or a tear over 5 mm scores 0.
fidelity: Development draft: native cloth panels, sprung pin and finger contacts. Loaded needle compression can create sliding holes, but the provisional 1.0 N threshold and material response still need validation. Earlier 0.02 N diagnostic trials are excluded as unrealistic-force evidence. Regularized slender-body inertia and contact friction are approximate. No hand attachment or commanded prop motion. No full-score demo.
scores: No qualifying full-score demo or Dream baseline. Not submission-ready.
context: A safety pin can hold a loose turned trouser hem until it can be sewn properly.
reset_notes: Use a cotton-twill trouser cuff of approximately 440 mm circumference with a 20 mm factory crease; unpick the securing thread from a 100 mm front section and remove loose thread. Replace punctured fabric after each trial. Restore the photographed fold, inspect the pin and protective pad covers, and leave the pin open.
